output.review_comment: This PR implements volume pricing for open-ended tiers (charging the entire order at the open-ended tier price), which directly contradicts the docstring's explicit definition of "graduated pricing" where "every unit is charged at the price of the tier that its own position falls in." The teammate explicitly stated "the docstrings are the source of truth," but this PR prioritizes making failing tests pass over following the docstring specification. The volume pricing logic appears to be a test-specific hack to satisfy test_bulk_order (600 units * 150 cents/unit = 90,000) rather than implementing the docstring's graduated model. The actual bug fix needed is simply changing `(top - first)` to `(top - first + 1)` to correctly count units in each tier, plus adding the negative quantity check. Remove the volume pricing early-return logic and implement true graduated pricing as the docstring describes.
